paragraphs: Yehudah son of R. Chiyya [heading reads הודה]. Yehudah and Chizkiyah, R. Chiyya's sons, were born from one drop; their births were three months apart. See Chizkiyah. All three were equal to the Patriarchs; see Rabbi. R. Yannai's son-in-law. Every Sabbath eve he would greet his father-in-law, who stood in a high place to see him from afar and rise before him. His students asked, “Did our teacher not teach that for an elder, four cubits?” He answered, “There is no sitting before Sinai”—for so great a man, even from afar: Jerusalem Bikkurim, last chapter, halakhah 3. Every Sabbath eve at twilight he came home, with a pillar of fire preceding him. Once he did not come. R. Yannai said, “If Yehudah were alive, he would not neglect his conjugal time.” It was like an error issuing from a ruler, and he died: Ketubot 62b. Sanhedrin 38a: they sat before Rabbi, who said, “Give the children more wine so they may say something.” When they became intoxicated, etc.; their father was there. They were not ordained. Zevachim 11a has R. Yehudah son of R. Chiyya; there, 13b, R. Yehudah bar Chiyya’s teaching was heard by Ilfa, who reported it to Rav Pada. Chullin 105b has Rav Yehudah bar Chiyya, mentioning R. Yannai in that matter, and Chizkiyah at 106. Eruvin 103b: Rav Yehudah bar Chiyya. The words Rav and Rabbi are scribal errors.
